note: Messages for humanize.py and detect.py: every sentence they print, as str.format templates. Not the lexicon (slop.en.json), so --lexicon never swaps them.

messages.hanging_name: Deleting "{find}" would leave the sentence hanging
messages.hanging_fix: Rewrite the sentence without the phrase. Deleting it alone leaves a fragment ("If you love design.").
messages.role_name: No plain word fits "{find}" here, so it was kept
messages.role_fix: Rewrite the sentence around it. One word cannot stand in for it in this use ("an empowering talk" is not "a helping talk").
messages.uniform_fix: Break one sentence in half. Let another run long. Machines write even.
messages.report_summary: {total} machine artefacts removed, {tells} structural tells flagged for rewrite
messages.section_structural:
4. STRUCTURAL TELLS  (not auto-fixed - rewrite these yourself)
--------------------------------------------------------------

messages.fingerprint_detail: {invisible} invisible, {em} em dash, {curly} curly quote, {ellipsis} ellipsis, {nbsp} hard space
messages.voice_detail: {contractions:.1f} contractions, {person:.1f} personal pronouns per 100 words, {tells} structural tell(s)
messages.held_at_review: Held at REVIEW: {tells} structural tell(s) left. Rewrite them by hand; humanize.py --report lists them.
messages.held_uncalibrated: Held at REVIEW: the {lang} lexicon is not calibrated yet, so no draft passes. Read it yourself.

concrete.note: What counts as concrete, the same in hookscore, beats, caption and detect (tests/test_concrete.py keeps this section equal in ig-reel, ig-caption and ig-human). months leaves out "may": it is a verb far more often. caps_skip: all-caps words that are not a place or a thing.
